{{Short description|Gas condensation following the Big Bang}}
A '''Zeldovich pancake''' is a theoretical condensation of gas out of a [[wikt:primordial|primordial]] density fluctuation following the [[Big Bang]]. In 1970, [[Yakov Borisovich Zel'dovich|Yakov B. Zeldovich]] showed that for an [[ellipsoid]] of gas on a [[wikt:supergalaxy|supergalactic]] scale, an approximation can be used that will model the collapse as occurring most rapidly along the shortest axis, resulting in a pancake form.<ref>{{cite book
 | first=M. S. | last=Longair | date=2007
 | title=Galaxy Formation | publisher=Springer
 | pages=475–476 | isbn=978-3-540-73477-2
}}</ref> This approximation assumes that the [[ellipsoid]] of gas is sufficiently large that the effect of pressure is negligible and only [[gravity|gravitational]] attraction needs to be considered. That is, the gas will collapse without being significantly perturbed by outward pressure. This assumption is especially valid if the collapse occurs before the [[recombination (cosmology)|recombination]] era that resulted in the formation of [[hydrogen]] atoms.<ref>{{cite journal
 | first=Y. B. | last=Zeldovich | date=1970
 | title=Gravitational instability: an approximate theory for large density perturbations
 | journal=[[Astronomy and Astrophysics]] | volume=5
 | pages=84–89 | bibcode=1970A&A.....5...84Z }}</ref>

In 1989, Zeldovich and S. F. Shandarin showed that initial overlapping density fluctuations of random Gaussian fields would result in "dense pancakes, filaments, and compact clumps of matter".<ref>{{cite journal
 | author=Shandarin, S. F.
 | author2=Zeldovich, Ya. B.
 | title=The large-scale structure of the universe: Turbulence, intermittency, structures in a self-gravitating medium | journal=[[Reviews of Modern Physics]]
 | volume=61 | issue=2 | date=1989
 | pages=185–220 | doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.61.185 | bibcode=1989RvMP...61..185S
}}</ref> This model became known as a top-down model of galactic formation, with the supergalactic condensation fragmenting into [[protogalaxies]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | author=Subramanian, Kandaswamy
 | author2=Swarup, Govind
 | title=A cluster of protogalaxies at redshift 3.4?
 | journal=Nature | volume=359 | issue=6395
 | pages=512–514 | doi=10.1038/359512a0
 | date=1992 |bibcode = 1992Natur.359..512S | s2cid=4258493
 }}</ref> The formation of plane concentrations would compress the gas through [[shock wave]]s generated during the collapse, increasing the temperature.<ref>{{cite journal
 | author=Sunyaev, R. A.
 | author2=Zeldovich, Ya. B.
 | title=Formation of Clusters of Galaxies; Protocluster Fragmentation and Intergalactic Gas Heating | journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics
 | volume=20 | pages=189–200 |date=August 1972
 | bibcode=1972A&A....20..189S
}}</ref>

At a higher level, the collapse of larger structures according to the [[Zeldovich approximation]] is known as second-generation pancakes or superpancakes. At still higher levels there is a transition to a hierarchical clustering model in which a hierarchy of collapsing structures exist. The Truncated Zeldovich Approximation allowed the method to be applied to these hierarchical, or bottom-up models of cosmological structure. This approach truncates the power law [[fluctuation spectrum]] at large values of ''k'' before applying the Zeldovich Approximation.<ref>{{cite journal
  | author=Pauls, Jennifer L.
  | author2=Melott, Adrian L.
  | title=Hierarchical pancaking: why the Zel'dovich approximation describes coherent large-scale structure in N-body simulations of gravitational clustering
  | journal=[[Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society]] | volume=274 | issue=1 | pages=99–109
  |date=May 1995 | bibcode=1995MNRAS.274...99P |arxiv = astro-ph/9408019 | doi=10.1093/mnras/274.1.99| doi-access=free
 }}</ref> Generalizations of the Zel'dovich Approximation have also been shown to apply in the case of a non-zero [[cosmological constant]].<ref>{{cite journal
  | author=Barrow, John D.
  | author2=Goetz, Guenter
  | title=Newtonian no-hair theorems
  | journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity
  | volume=6 |date=September 1989
  | issue=9
  | pages=1253–1265 | doi=10.1088/0264-9381/6/9/010 |bibcode = 1989CQGra...6.1253B }}</ref>

The first example of a Zeldovich pancake may have been identified in 1991 using the [[Very Large Array]] in [[New Mexico]].<ref>{{cite news
 | first=John Noble | last=Wilford | date=1991-12-10
 | title=Giant 'Pancake' Is Clue To Origin of Universe
 | work=[[The New York Times]]
 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/12/10/science/giant-pancake-is-clue-to-origin-of-universe.html?sec=health&spon=&pagewanted=all | access-date=2009-04-20
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 | author=Uson, Juan M.
 | author2=Bagri, Durgadas S.
 | author3=Cornwell, Timothy J. | title=Radio detections of neutral hydrogen at redshift Z=3.4
 | journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] | volume=67
 | issue=24 | date=1991-12-09 | pages=3328–3331
 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.3328
 | pmid=10044706 | bibcode=1991PhRvL..67.3328U}}</ref>
